content: Raltegravir is a medication used in combination with other HIV drugs to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which allows the immune system to function more effectively. This, in turn, lowers the risk of developing complications related to HIV, such as new infections or certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Raltegravir belongs to a class of drugs known as integrase inhibitors. However, it is important to note that raltegravir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, it is essential to take all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Additionally, you should use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items that may come into contact with blood or other body fluids, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors. Before starting raltegravir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it each time you get a refill. The dosage of raltegravir is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Swallow the medication whole, as directed by the manufacturer. While some similar drugs (immediate-release tablets) can be split or crushed, follow your doctor’s instructions regarding raltegravir. Avoid using antacids containing aluminum or magnesium while taking this medication. It is crucial to continue taking raltegravir and other HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Similarly, do not reduce your dose or stop taking it, even for a short time, unless instructed to do so by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects of raltegravir may include headache, nausea, and difficulty sleeping. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Changes in body fat distribution may also occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Serious allergic reactions to raltegravir are rare. If you experience any side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada. Before taking raltegravir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, raltegravir should only be used when clearly needed. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of passing the infection to your baby, and raltegravir may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding. Drug interactions may affect how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking raltegravir, regular lab and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, should be performed to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store raltegravir in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the drying agent (desiccant) in the bottle and tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about raltegravir. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
